JP:CN.source_name: National Immigration Administration — Unilateral Visa-Free Country List (as at 17 February 2026)
JP:CN.note: Japan is on China's unilateral visa-free list (National Immigration Administration list published 17 February 2026): holders of ordinary passports may enter without a visa for up to 30 days for business, tourism, family or friends visits, exchange visits or transit, with the stay counted from the day after entry. Work, study and residence are not covered. The scheme is temporary and currently runs until 31 December 2026.

US:JP.source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan — Exemption of Visa (Short-Term Stay)
US:JP.note: No visa is required for a short-term stay of up to 90 days for tourism, business or visiting friends or relatives. Landing permission is granted by an immigration officer on arrival; a visa exemption does not guarantee entry.

CN:SG.source_name: Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) — visa requirements & Assessment Level lists
CN:SG.note: China passport holders enter Singapore visa-free; the visit pass granted on arrival allows up to 30 days. The exemption rests on the China–Singapore mutual visa-exemption arrangement in force since 9 February 2024, covering ordinary passports. Every traveller must also submit the free SG Arrival Card online within 3 days before arrival — ICA states expressly that the card is not a visa.

US:CN.source_name: National Immigration Administration — Visa-Free Transit Policy (240-hour scheme, 57 countries; Hainan scheme, 61 countries)
US:CN.note: A Chinese visa is required in advance — apply through a Chinese Visa Application Service Center or a Chinese embassy or consulate (fees, validity and number of entries vary by nationality and reciprocity). Most nationalities can transit China airside for up to 24 hours without a visa, but a visa is always needed to enter China as the destination; work, study and residence need the matching visa category. United States is one of the 57 nationalities eligible for China's 240-hour (10-day) visa-free transit: with a confirmed onward ticket to a third country or territory, travellers may enter at 65 designated ports across 24 provinces and stay within the designated areas for up to 240 hours — for transit only, not for visiting China as the destination. Separately, United States passport holders may enter Hainan Province without a visa for up to 30 days under the Hainan visa-free scheme (61 countries) — valid for Hainan only, not for the rest of mainland China.

SG:GB.source_name: Immigration Rules Appendix ETA National List (GOV.UK)
SG:GB.note: Get an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) online or in the UK ETA app before travelling — fee £20 since 8 April 2026 (£16 from 9 April 2025, £10 at launch). An approved ETA is valid for 2 years or until the passport expires, allows multiple journeys, and each stay as a Visitor may be up to 6 months. An ETA is permission to travel, not a guarantee of admission — the Border Force officer decides on arrival. Apply on the passport you will travel with. Since 25 February 2026 carriers must check permission to travel before boarding. Coming to marry, form a civil partnership or give notice of marriage in the UK always needs a Marriage/Civil Partnership Visitor visa in advance — an ETA does not cover it.

SG:FR.source_name: France-Visas — official visa portal of the French MFA and Ministry of the Interior
SG:FR.note: Visa-free for short stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen Area as a whole — the clock covers all Schengen states combined (Annex II of EU Regulation 2018/1806, which France applies for its European territory). Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure and issued within the previous 10 years; border officers may ask for the purpose of the stay, sufficient funds and return or onward proof. This covers metropolitan (European) France; France's overseas departments and territories have separate entry rules, and a Schengen visa or exemption does not automatically cover them.

CN:NL.source_name: Netherlands Schengen visa list (NederlandWereldwijd / IND) — Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806
CN:NL.note: A short-stay Schengen (uniform) visa is required in advance: file at VFS Global or TLScontact — the application is decided by the Consular Service Organisation of the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs in The Hague, averaging 18 to 21 calendar days (legal range 15 days, up to 45). Fee EUR 90; apply between 6 months and at least 15 days before travel. A uniform visa issued by any Schengen state is valid for the Netherlands, and holders of a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by another Schengen state may enter without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure, with two blank pages, issued within the previous 10 years. This covers the European part of the Netherlands; the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom (Aruba, Bonaire, Curaçao, Saba, Sint Eustatius and Sint Maarten) have their own entry rules.

KR:EG.source_name: Wikipedia — Visa policy of Egypt (IATA Timatic)
KR:EG.note: Visa on arrival for tourism, up to 30 days. Buy at the airport before immigration for US$30 in cash; since August 2026 Cairo airport also sells a US$36 digital QR visa (card payment) via self-service machines or the Visa on Arrival portal. Your passport must be valid at least 6 months beyond arrival and have at least one blank page. Alternatively, apply for a tourist e-Visa online before travel at visa2egypt.gov.eg (single entry US$30, valid 90 days; multiple entry US$65, valid 180 days; each stay up to 30 days).

IL:EG.source_name: Embassy of Egypt in Washington — visa requirements
IL:EG.note: A visa must be obtained in advance with pre-approval from Egypt: applications are by email only, walk-ins are not accepted, and the Washington embassy quotes a minimum of 6–8 weeks for the first stage. Do not make travel plans until approval is received. Pre-approval nationals cannot obtain any visa on arrival, including holders of a US green card. Exception: entering only the South Sinai resorts (Sharm El Sheikh, Dahab, Nuweiba, Taba) via the Taba land crossing or direct flights to Sharm El Sheikh or Taba airports gives a free Sinai-only entry stamp (14 days per the UK consulate, 15 days per Timatic); it cannot be extended and does not permit travel to Cairo or the rest of Egypt.

SG:IL.source_name: Wikipedia - Visa policy of Israel (Timatic-based exemption table; ETA-IL rules per gov.il/PIBA)
SG:IL.note: Visa-exempt for up to 90 days (30 days for culture or sport activities). An approved ETA-IL is mandatory before travel since 1 January 2025: apply via the PIBA portal at least 72 hours ahead (fee ILS 25, valid 2 years or to passport expiry, multiple entries). Approval does not guarantee entry; the border officer decides. Passport validity: 3 months beyond arrival is the official ETA-IL rule, but airlines commonly enforce 6 months, so carry 6 months to be safe. An in-country extension of up to 90 days may be applied for. Note: the Embassy of Israel in Singapore's October 2026 eVisa-B2 notice also lists this nationality for online visas; the exemption plus ETA-IL is followed (the MFA table and the current exemption table agree) and the eVisa listing is treated as a duplicate/erroneous entry.

SG:KE.source_name: Kenya eTA portal — general information and eTA exemption list (etakenya.go.ke)
SG:KE.note: Exempt from Kenya’s eTA requirement under Legal Notice No. 93 of 2025 — no eTA and no visa needed for a stay of up to 90 days. Final admission is decided by the border officer on arrival.

KR:KE.source_name: Kenya eTA portal — general information and eTA exemption list (etakenya.go.ke)
KR:KE.note: Kenya replaced visas with an Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) in 2024. Apply at etakenya.go.ke before departure (US$30; usually decided within 3 working days — the portal recommends applying at least 2 weeks ahead). An approved eTA allows a stay of up to 90 days; it is permission to travel, and final admission is decided at the border.

The visa is a multiple-entry holiday visa for up to 90 days in a calendar year; fee N$1,600 (African Union passports N$1,200). A further N$400 surcharge for manual at-the-border applications has been approved but its start date had not been announced as of the Ministry's September 2025 notice.

GB:CN.source_name: National Immigration Administration — Unilateral Visa-Free Country List (as at 17 February 2026)
GB:CN.note: United Kingdom was added to China's unilateral visa-free list on 17 February 2026 (Ministry of Foreign Affairs announcement of 15 February 2026): holders of ordinary passports may enter without a visa for up to 30 days for business, tourism, family or friends visits, exchange visits or transit, with the stay counted from the day after entry. Work, study and residence are not covered. The scheme is temporary and currently runs until 31 December 2026.

CZ:CN.source_name: National Immigration Administration — Visa-Free Transit Policy (240-hour scheme, 57 countries; Hainan scheme, 61 countries)
CZ:CN.note: A Chinese visa is required in advance — apply through a Chinese Visa Application Service Center or a Chinese embassy or consulate (fees, validity and number of entries vary by nationality and reciprocity). Most nationalities can transit China airside for up to 24 hours without a visa, but a visa is always needed to enter China as the destination; work, study and residence need the matching visa category. Czechia is one of the 57 nationalities eligible for China's 240-hour (10-day) visa-free transit: with a confirmed onward ticket to a third country or territory, travellers may enter at 65 designated ports across 24 provinces and stay within the designated areas for up to 240 hours — for transit only, not for visiting China as the destination. Separately, Czechia passport holders may enter Hainan Province without a visa for up to 30 days under the Hainan visa-free scheme (61 countries) — valid for Hainan only, not for the rest of mainland China.

IL:CN.note: A Chinese visa is required in advance — apply through a Chinese Visa Application Service Center or a Chinese embassy or consulate (fees, validity and number of entries vary by nationality and reciprocity). SG:US.source_name: U.S. Department of State — Visa Waiver Program
SG:US.note: Travel under the Visa Waiver Program (VWP): get an ESTA authorisation from CBP online before boarding — fee USD 40.62 since 16 October 2026 (USD 40 from 30 September 2025, USD 21 before that); an approved ESTA is normally valid for two years or until the passport expires. Stays of up to 90 days for tourism or business; the stay cannot be extended and status cannot be changed, and an approved ESTA does not guarantee admission — the CBP officer at the port of entry decides. An e-passport is required. Travellers who have been in North Korea, Iran, Iraq, Libya, Somalia, Sudan, Syria or Yemen on or after 1 March 2011, or in Cuba on or after 12 January 2021, and dual nationals of Cuba, North Korea, Iran, Iraq, Sudan or Syria, cannot use the VWP and need a visitor visa instead.

IL:US.source_name: U.S. Department of State — Visa Waiver Program
IL:US.note: Travel under the Visa Waiver Program (VWP): get an ESTA authorisation from CBP online before boarding — fee USD 40.62 since 16 October 2026 (USD 40 from 30 September 2025, USD 21 before that); an approved ESTA is normally valid for two years or until the passport expires. Stays of up to 90 days for tourism or business; the stay cannot be extended and status cannot be changed, and an approved ESTA does not guarantee admission — the CBP officer at the port of entry decides. An e-passport is required. Travellers who have been in North Korea, Iran, Iraq, Libya, Somalia, Sudan, Syria or Yemen on or after 1 March 2011, or in Cuba on or after 12 January 2021, and dual nationals of Cuba, North Korea, Iran, Iraq, Sudan or Syria, cannot use the VWP and need a visitor visa instead.

IL:MA.source_name: Morocco — Accès Maroc e-Visa terms (Category A)
IL:MA.note: Israel is a Category A e-Visa nationality under Morocco's official e-Visa terms: apply at acces-maroc.ma before travel. The e-Visa is single-entry, valid up to 180 days from issuance, for a stay of up to 30 days, for tourism or business only; standard processing 72 hours, express 24 hours (Moroccan working days). It cannot be extended into residence, and multiple e-Visas cannot be combined to extend a stay. The portal's checkout fee is reported as 770 MAD standard / 1,100 MAD express, while the 2025 gazette tariff lists 70 / 100 MAD — check the portal at application.

MV:IN.source_name: India–Maldives Visa Facilitation Agreement, 2018 (Ministry of External Affairs)
MV:IN.note: Under the 2018 India–Maldives visa facilitation agreement: stays of up to 90 days in total within any 180-day period, for tourism, business or medical visits.

AF:PK.source_name: Pakistan Online Visa System — tourist visa (visa.nadra.gov.pk)
AF:PK.note: Applications from Afghan passport holders go through mandatory inter-agency security screening, with processing of at least four weeks rather than the standard 7–10 working days.

SO:PK.source_name: Pakistan Online Visa System — tourist visa (visa.nadra.gov.pk)
SO:PK.note: Applications from Somali passport holders go through mandatory inter-agency security screening, with processing of at least four weeks rather than the standard 7–10 working days.

IN:PK.source_name: Directorate General of Immigration & Passports — visa for Indian nationals (dgip.gov.pk)
IN:PK.note: Indian nationals are outside the standard online tourist visa system. Under the bilateral arrangement, tourist visas are non-extendable, valid for 14 days, and issued only through approved tour operators by the Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi; visitor visas cover visits to relatives or friends and bona fide business (6 months, up to 3 entries). Entry and exit are only via designated check posts, police registration is required within 24 hours, and the passport must be valid for at least one year.

IL:PK.source_name: Directorate General of Immigration & Passports — visa categories (dgip.gov.pk)
IL:PK.note: Pakistan does not recognise Israel and Israeli passports are not accepted; no visa is issued to Israeli citizens through any channel.

AU:BD.source_name: Special Branch, Bangladesh Police — visa on arrival information (voa.specialbranch.gov.bd)
AU:BD.note: Visa on arrival for tourism or business at Dhaka, Chattogram and Sylhet international airports and designated land ports: 30 days, single entry, fee payable in foreign currency (standard US$50, reciprocity applies). Show at least US$500 in cash or card, a confirmed return ticket and accommodation, and use the same port for entry and departure.

IN:BD.source_name: Deputy High Commission of Bangladesh, Chennai — visa on arrival (chennai.mofa.gov.bd)
IN:BD.note: Visa on arrival is expressly not applicable for Indian nationals (“Visa on Arrival in Bangladesh is not applicable for Indian Nationals” — Bangladesh Deputy High Commission, Chennai). Indian tourists must obtain a visa in advance through a Bangladesh mission (application form via visa.gov.bd); the consular visa fee is waived for Indian citizens under reciprocity.

PK:BD.note: Pakistani nationals are not eligible for visa on arrival and cannot use the no-resident-mission route (Bangladesh maintains missions in Pakistan). A visa must be obtained in advance through a Bangladesh mission, and applications are referred for a security opinion before issuance.

IL:BD.source_name: Special Branch, Bangladesh Police — visa on arrival information (voa.specialbranch.gov.bd)

AD:KE.source_name: Kenya eTA portal — general information and eTA exemption list (etakenya.go.ke)
AD:KE.note: Kenya replaced visas with an Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) in 2024. Apply at etakenya.go.ke before departure (US$30; usually decided within 3 working days — the portal recommends applying at least 2 weeks ahead). An approved eTA allows a stay of up to 90 days; it is permission to travel, and final admission is decided at the border.

Apply at etakenya.go.ke before departure (US$30; usually decided within 3 working days — the portal recommends applying at least 2 weeks ahead). An approved eTA allows a stay of up to 90 days; it is permission to travel, and final admission is decided at the border.

CD:BI.source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Burundi) — free visas: EAC & CEPGL access visas (mae.gov.bi)
CD:BI.note: The DR Congo is exempt from visa application for Burundi (it is named on the official embassy exemption list) and qualifies for the free CEPGL access visa, valid for up to three months. Burundi does not treat Congolese citizens under the EAC access-visa category — the EAC's own FAQ exempts EAC nationals “with the exception of DRC”, and the migration authority charges Congolese students a separate visa fee — so the CEPGL three-month validity is used here.

The tourist e-Visa is issued for a stay of 30, 60 or 90 days (30 days is shown here), is multiple-entry and valid for two months from issue; standard processing is about five business days.

The ETA allows multiple entries and a stay of up to 30 days, extendable once by a further 30 days.

AD:CD.source_name: Direction Générale de Migration — e-Visa FAQ: Visa Volant and the 7-day airport visa (evisa.gouv.cd)
AD:CD.note: A visa must be obtained before travel. The standard route is a Visa de Voyage from a Congolese embassy (validity 1 to 6 months, single or multiple entry; a Congolese sponsor's undertaking — prise en charge — and a yellow-fever vaccination certificate are required). The migration service also runs an e-Visa portal (evisa.gouv.cd) selling a Visa Volant pre-approval — US$300 online, of which US$50 is a non-refundable fee, processed in about 72 hours — which converts on arrival into a 7-day airport/port visa (US$90 at the border, single entry, extendable with the DGM). That online channel is designed for travellers from countries without a Congolese embassy; it is not the standard tourist visa.

The migration service also runs an e-Visa portal (evisa.gouv.cd) selling a Visa Volant pre-approval — US$300 online, of which US$50 is a non-refundable fee, processed in about 72 hours — which converts on arrival into a 7-day airport/port visa (US$90 at the border, single entry, extendable with the DGM). That online channel is designed for travellers from countries without a Congolese embassy; it is not the standard tourist visa.

That online channel is designed for travellers from countries without a Congolese embassy; it is not the standard tourist visa.

The standard route is a Visa de Voyage from a Congolese embassy (validity 1 to 6 months, single or multiple entry; a Congolese sponsor's undertaking — prise en charge — and a yellow-fever vaccination certificate are required). The migration service also runs an e-Visa portal (evisa.gouv.cd) selling a Visa Volant pre-approval — US$300 online, of which US$50 is a non-refundable fee, processed in about 72 hours — which converts on arrival into a 7-day airport/port visa (US$90 at the border, single entry, extendable with the DGM). That online channel is designed for travellers from countries without a Congolese embassy; it is not the standard tourist visa.

RW:CD.source_name: Rwanda DGIE — travel assistance: visa not required (migration.gov.rw)
RW:CD.note: Citizens of Rwanda enter the DR Congo without a visa under the CEPGL arrangements and East African Community membership — Rwanda's immigration service states 'visa not required' for Congolese travel in both directions. No official Congolese or EAC text states a maximum stay for this exemption, so no stay is shown here.

TD:CD.source_name: Government of the DR Congo — Council of Ministers record, 28 June 2024 (primature.gouv.cd)

The migration service has not published an implementing circular, so travellers may wish to confirm current practice before departure.

AD:SS.source_name: South Sudan Trade Information Hub — 'Obtain entry visa - online', step 1: apply and pay for entry visa (DCNPI procedure, updated June 2026)
AD:SS.note: South Sudan's visa is obtained before travel on the official e-Visa portal (evisa.gov.ss): create an account, apply and pay online, then download the visa PDF within about 72 hours; it is checked at the port of entry in about five minutes and the passport is stamped. Fees are set by the visa's validity, not by a permitted stay: US$100 single entry, US$200 for 3-month multiple entry and US$350 for 6-month multiple entry, plus a US$15 entry-permit fee (Trade Information Hub procedure under the Financial Act 2024/25). A coloured invitation letter and a yellow-fever vaccination certificate are required. No official source states a maximum stay per entry — the 3- and 6-month figures are validity periods — so no stay is shown here. There is no walk-up visa on arrival, and airlines are penalised for carrying passengers who arrive without a visa.

Fees are set by the visa's validity, not by a permitted stay: US$100 single entry, US$200 for 3-month multiple entry and US$350 for 6-month multiple entry, plus a US$15 entry-permit fee (Trade Information Hub procedure under the Financial Act 2024/25). A coloured invitation letter and a yellow-fever vaccination certificate are required. No official source states a maximum stay per entry — the 3- and 6-month figures are validity periods — so no stay is shown here. There is no walk-up visa on arrival, and airlines are penalised for carrying passengers who arrive without a visa.

AD:SO.source_name: Somalia Immigration and Citizenship Agency — launch of the E-Visa/ETAS system, effective 1 September 2025 (immigration.gov.so)
AD:SO.note: Since 1 September 2025 every foreign visitor must obtain Somalia's E-Visa/ETAS online before travel (etas.gov.so) — visa on arrival was abolished at federal ports of entry, and there are no visa exemptions for ordinary passports, including for East African Community partner states (Somalia joined the EAC in 2024 but has not implemented Common Market visa-free movement). Somali federal pages publish no maximum stay or fee: the stay of up to 30 days from entry, the US$64 fee and roughly seven days' processing are stated by the Czech Ministry of Foreign Affairs' official travel information. Apply well ahead — and note that in November 2025 the US Embassy and the UK Foreign Office warned that the e-Visa system had suffered a data breach exposing applicants' personal data, and advised travellers to consider the risk before applying.

Somali federal pages publish no maximum stay or fee: the stay of up to 30 days from entry, the US$64 fee and roughly seven days' processing are stated by the Czech Ministry of Foreign Affairs' official travel information. Apply well ahead — and note that in November 2025 the US Embassy and the UK Foreign Office warned that the e-Visa system had suffered a data breach exposing applicants' personal data, and advised travellers to consider the risk before applying.

AD:AO.source_name: Embassy of Angola — visa-exempt countries and the simplified tourist-visa procedure under Presidential Decree 189/23 (angola.org)
AD:AO.note: Everyone not on Angola's exemption lists needs a tourist visa — but the process is simplified by law: apply online through the Migration Service (SME) e-Visa portal (evisa.ao) or at an Angolan embassy, with a decision due within three working days (Presidential Decree 189/23, Article 4). Use the visa within 60 days of issue; the stay is up to 30 days, extendable once. There is no walk-up visa on arrival for tourists — the 'tourist visa issued at the border' in the fee table is the second step of the advance online procedure, not an arrival facility, and the separate 15-day emergency border visa covers documented emergencies (such as urgent technical work), not tourism. Fees are set in kwanza by law (21,350 Kz at a consulate, 36,600 Kz for the border-issued step) and Angola publishes no official dollar or euro prices, so treat any converted price with caution.

Visitors may stay up to 90 days in any 12 months, though the full amount is not always granted on first entry. Bring your host's full address, a passport with at least six months' validity and three blank pages, and (if flying) a return ticket. If your trip crosses into Zimbabwe, the KAZA UNIVISA (US$50, sold at Lusaka and Livingstone airports, the Victoria Falls and Kazungula borders) covers both countries for up to 30 days with multiple crossings, plus day trips into Botswana via Kazungula.

US:ML.source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Mali — communiqués of 30 December 2025 and 2 January 2026 (reciprocal suspension of US citizens' entry)
US:ML.note: Entry of United States citizens to Mali is SUSPENDED: by Foreign Ministry communiqués of 30 December 2025 and 2 January 2026, Mali applied reciprocity for the US restrictions on Malian citizens — since 1 January 2026 US ordinary passport holders cannot enter and Malian missions have stopped issuing them new visas. Exempt: Mali permanent residents, holders of still-valid visas, diplomats, athletes and cases approved in Mali's national interest. The embassy fee page ($185, visas up to 5 years) predates the suspension and has not been updated. The decision is stated to be under review, not permanent.

There is no e-Visa (no official portal exists) and no visa on arrival; the only arrival exception ('visa volant') is for travellers from countries with no Nigerien mission and needs prior approval in Niamey, on unpublished terms.

US:NE.source_name: Agence Nigérienne de Presse (ANP), 25 December 2025 — Niger bars visas and entry to US citizens
US:NE.note: United States citizens are BARRED from Niger: on 25 December 2025 Niger announced — via its official press agency, in reciprocity for the US entry restrictions on Nigeriens of 16 December 2025 — a complete and indefinite prohibition on issuing visas to US citizens and on their entry, effective immediately. This followed the Washington embassy's suspension of ordinary visas in August 2025. The announcements do not address already-valid visas or diplomatic travel.

AD:BF.source_name: eVisaburkina — official e-Visa portal of Burkina Faso (Ministry of Security, since 1 February 2023)

Entry is under the ECOWAS free-movement framework (protocol stay: 90 days); Guinea keeps the AES states Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger exempt on the live portal even after their ECOWAS exit.

NI:GN.source_name: DCPAF e-Visa portal of Guinea (paf.gov.gn) — nationality list and travel information
NI:GN.note: Citizens of Nicaragua must apply online before travelling on Guinea's official e-Visa portal (paf.gov.gn): approval comes as an entry-visa letter, and the visa itself is issued on arrival at Conakry airport (or another designated post) after biometrics. The short-stay tourist e-Visa allows up to 90 days and costs US$100. There is no walk-up visa on arrival without the approved letter.

AD:GW.source_name: French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs — Guinea-Bissau travel advice (entry conditions, conditional airport visa)
AD:GW.note: Citizens of Andorra need a visa for Guinea-Bissau, normally obtained in advance from a Guinea-Bissau embassy — the old e-Visa website is defunct and there is no official online application. A visa CAN be issued at Bissau airport, but only conditionally: a local contact must notify the immigration service in advance (or it is an emergency, or there is no Guinea-Bissau mission in your country of residence), airlines may refuse boarding without the prior authorisation, the fee is paid in cash, and no official stay or fee is published.

AD:SL.source_name: Sierra Leone National Tourist Board — Visa on Arrival policy notice (effective 5 September 2019)
AD:SL.note: Andorra is not listed in the Sierra Leone National Tourist Board's visa-on-arrival policy notice (effective 5 September 2019) and no visa-free agreement between Sierra Leone and Andorra has been published, so Andorra citizens must obtain a visa from a Sierra Leone embassy or mission before travel — the course the notice directs for unlisted countries. Sierra Leone's e-Visa portal (evisa.sl, live since March 2023) publishes no nationality eligibility list and no official source confirms whether Andorra citizens may use it, so the mission channel is the settled route. Travel for purposes other than tourism, visits or business always requires a visa in advance.

AE:SL.source_name: Sierra Leone National Tourist Board — Visa on Arrival policy notice (effective 5 September 2019)
AE:SL.note: Sierra Leone's visa-on-arrival policy (National Tourist Board notice, effective 5 September 2019) makes United Arab Emirates citizens eligible for a visa on arrival: citizens of Gulf Cooperation Council member countries are listed in the notice. The fee is US$80, payable in US-dollar cash on arrival; the same visa can be pre-arranged through the official e-Visa portal (evisa.sl), which issues an approval that is formalised on arrival. The Tourist Board's notice publishes no maximum stay; the 30 days shown is the maximum stay of a single-entry visitor or business visa — valid 90 days from issue, with multiple-entry visas running 365 days at 30 days per visit — as stated in the UK FCDO's Sierra Leone entry guidance. Arrival visas cover tourism, visits and business only; other purposes need a visa in advance. All arrivals must hold a yellow-fever vaccination certificate and complete Sierra Leone's health declaration within 72 hours before travel. The UAE's visa-exemption arrangement with Sierra Leone covers diplomatic and special passports only; ordinary passports are not exempt.

The fee is US$80, payable in US-dollar cash on arrival; the same visa can be pre-arranged through the official e-Visa portal (evisa.sl), which issues an approval that is formalised on arrival. The Tourist Board's notice publishes no maximum stay; the 30 days shown is the maximum stay of a single-entry visitor or business visa — valid 90 days from issue, with multiple-entry visas running 365 days at 30 days per visit — as stated in the UK FCDO's Sierra Leone entry guidance. Arrival visas cover tourism, visits and business only; other purposes need a visa in advance. All arrivals must hold a yellow-fever vaccination certificate and complete Sierra Leone's health declaration within 72 hours before travel.

Sierra Leone's visa-on-arrival policy (National Tourist Board notice, effective 5 September 2019) prices visas on arrival for non-ECOWAS AU nationals at US$25. The same visa can be pre-arranged through the official e-Visa portal (evisa.sl), which issues an approval that is formalised on arrival. The Tourist Board's notice publishes no maximum stay; the 30 days shown is the maximum stay of a single-entry visitor or business visa — valid 90 days from issue, with multiple-entry visas running 365 days at 30 days per visit — as stated in the UK FCDO's Sierra Leone entry guidance. Arrival visas cover tourism, visits and business only; other purposes need a visa in advance. All arrivals must hold a yellow-fever vaccination certificate and complete Sierra Leone's health declaration within 72 hours before travel.

AD:LR.source_name: Liberia Immigration Service — Visa on Arrival (e-Visa) portal (visaonarrival.lis.gov.lr)
AD:LR.note: Liberia's 'Visa on Arrival' is an online pre-approval, not a walk-up arrival visa: since 11 March 2025, travellers from Andorra must apply on the Liberia Immigration Service portal (visaonarrival.lis.gov.lr) at least 7 days before flying (fee US$102.50, non-refundable), and the visa sticker is issued after biometric enrolment on arrival at Roberts International Airport, Monrovia — the only entry point where the scheme operates; arriving by land or sea requires an embassy visa obtained in advance. The approval is single-entry and must be used within 3 months. The portal states that the officer at the airport sets the stay at 30 or 90 days according to the length of the visit; the 90 days shown is that published maximum. Andorra has no Liberian embassy, which is what makes its travellers eligible for the portal — anyone whose country hosts a Liberian embassy must apply there instead. Tourism, business and transit only; the Immigration Service reserves the right to decline an application. A yellow-fever vaccination certificate is required of all arrivals.

No Liberian official source publishes a maximum stay for exempt ECOWAS nationals, so no figure is shown (Japanese official guidance reports border officers handwriting 30 or 60 days on entry stamps in practice). A yellow-fever vaccination certificate is required of all arrivals.

NI:LR.source_name: Liberia Immigration Service — Visa on Arrival (e-Visa) portal (visaonarrival.lis.gov.lr)
NI:LR.note: Liberia's 'Visa on Arrival' is an online pre-approval, not a walk-up arrival visa: since 11 March 2025, travellers from Nicaragua must apply on the Liberia Immigration Service portal (visaonarrival.lis.gov.lr) at least 7 days before flying (fee US$102.50, non-refundable), and the visa sticker is issued after biometric enrolment on arrival at Roberts International Airport, Monrovia — the only entry point where the scheme operates; arriving by land or sea requires an embassy visa obtained in advance. The approval is single-entry and must be used within 3 months. The portal states that the officer at the airport sets the stay at 30 or 90 days according to the length of the visit; the 90 days shown is that published maximum. Nicaragua has no Liberian embassy, which is what makes its travellers eligible for the portal — anyone whose country hosts a Liberian embassy must apply there instead. Tourism, business and transit only; the Immigration Service reserves the right to decline an application. A yellow-fever vaccination certificate is required of all arrivals.

AD:CI.source_name: SNEDAI — E-visa (Côte d'Ivoire's official e-Visa portal)
AD:CI.note: Côte d'Ivoire's visa is biometric and there is no walk-up visa on arrival. Travellers from Andorra pre-register online with SNEDAI, the state-concessioned operator (snedai.com/e-visa), uploading the passport identity page, the return-ticket reservation and an invitation letter or accommodation certificate, and pay €73; the Direction de la Surveillance du Territoire decides, normally within 48 working hours, and the approval must be used within 3 months. The biometric visa sticker is printed and affixed only after fingerprint and photo enrolment at Abidjan airport's visa desk on arrival — so the e-Visa route works only for travellers flying into Abidjan; anyone entering Côte d'Ivoire by land or sea must hold a biometric visa from an Ivorian embassy or consulate obtained in advance (€50). The visa issued is a multiple-entry short-stay visa of 3 months' duration, the statutory ceiling for a short stay; the 90 days shown is that duration, and Ivorian texts publish no separate shorter per-entry cap. Arriving without pre-registration is exceptional and at the DST's discretion. A yellow-fever vaccination certificate is required of all arrivals.

The biometric visa sticker is printed and affixed only after fingerprint and photo enrolment at Abidjan airport's visa desk on arrival — so the e-Visa route works only for travellers flying into Abidjan; anyone entering Côte d'Ivoire by land or sea must hold a biometric visa from an Ivorian embassy or consulate obtained in advance (€50). The visa issued is a multiple-entry short-stay visa of 3 months' duration, the statutory ceiling for a short stay; the 90 days shown is that duration, and Ivorian texts publish no separate shorter per-entry cap. Arriving without pre-registration is exceptional and at the DST's discretion. A yellow-fever vaccination certificate is required of all arrivals.

Travellers from Kuwait pre-register online with SNEDAI, the state-concessioned operator (snedai.com/e-visa), uploading the passport identity page, the return-ticket reservation and an invitation letter or accommodation certificate, and pay €73; the Direction de la Surveillance du Territoire decides, normally within 48 working hours, and the approval must be used within 3 months. The biometric visa sticker is printed and affixed only after fingerprint and photo enrolment at Abidjan airport's visa desk on arrival — so the e-Visa route works only for travellers flying into Abidjan; anyone entering Côte d'Ivoire by land or sea must hold a biometric visa from an Ivorian embassy or consulate obtained in advance (€50). The visa issued is a multiple-entry short-stay visa of 3 months' duration, the statutory ceiling for a short stay; the 90 days shown is that duration, and Ivorian texts publish no separate shorter per-entry cap. Arriving without pre-registration is exceptional and at the DST's discretion. A yellow-fever vaccination certificate is required of all arrivals.

The biometric visa sticker is printed and affixed only after fingerprint and photo enrolment at Abidjan airport's visa desk on arrival — so the e-Visa route works only for travellers flying into Abidjan; anyone entering Côte d'Ivoire by land or sea must hold a biometric visa from an Ivorian embassy or consulate obtained in advance (€50). The visa issued is a multiple-entry short-stay visa of 3 months' duration, the statutory ceiling for a short stay; the 90 days shown is that duration, and Ivorian texts publish no separate shorter per-entry cap. Arriving without pre-registration is exceptional and at the DST's discretion. A yellow-fever vaccination certificate is required of all arrivals.

Travellers from Serbia pre-register online with SNEDAI, the state-concessioned operator (snedai.com/e-visa), uploading the passport identity page, the return-ticket reservation and an invitation letter or accommodation certificate, and pay €73; the Direction de la Surveillance du Territoire decides, normally within 48 working hours, and the approval must be used within 3 months. The biometric visa sticker is printed and affixed only after fingerprint and photo enrolment at Abidjan airport's visa desk on arrival — so the e-Visa route works only for travellers flying into Abidjan; anyone entering Côte d'Ivoire by land or sea must hold a biometric visa from an Ivorian embassy or consulate obtained in advance (€50). The visa issued is a multiple-entry short-stay visa of 3 months' duration, the statutory ceiling for a short stay; the 90 days shown is that duration, and Ivorian texts publish no separate shorter per-entry cap. Arriving without pre-registration is exceptional and at the DST's discretion. A yellow-fever vaccination certificate is required of all arrivals.

AD:TG.source_name: Voyage Togo (voyage.gouv.tg) — official travel platform, exempt-country table and visa fees
AD:TG.note: Togo abolished visas on arrival in 2022: travellers from Andorra must obtain an e-Visa before travelling on the Togo Voyage platform (voyage.gouv.tg) — apply at least 5 working days ahead (standard processing up to 5 working days), pay online only (Visa/Mastercard or TMoney/Flooz; cash is not accepted), and note that travellers without an approved visa are turned back at the border. Tourist visas are sold by duration: 1–15 days single entry 25,000 FCFA, 1–15 days multiple entry 35,000 FCFA, 16–30 days 45,000 FCFA and 31–90 days 65,000 FCFA — the 90 days shown is the maximum tourist stay. The e-Visa is valid at air, land and sea borders alike, and Togolese embassies no longer issue routine paper visas. A yellow-fever vaccination certificate is mandatory.

AO:TG.source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Togo — visa exemption for African nationals (May 2026)
AO:TG.note: Angola citizens are visa-exempt under Togo's decree of 26 May 2026, which exempts nationals of all African states holding a valid passport for stays of up to 30 days; stays beyond 30 days require an e-Visa obtained in advance on voyage.gouv.tg. The platform's static country tables predate the decree and still list Angola among the e-Visa countries. Like all arrivals, exempt travellers must still complete the free immigration formalities online on voyage.gouv.tg before travelling — under the 2026 decree the travel declaration must be filed at least 24 hours before arrival to obtain the bordereau presented at the border post. A yellow-fever vaccination certificate is mandatory.

AR:TG.source_name: Voyage Togo (voyage.gouv.tg) — official travel platform, exempt-country table and visa fees
AR:TG.note: Togo abolished visas on arrival in 2022: travellers from Argentina must obtain an e-Visa before travelling on the Togo Voyage platform (voyage.gouv.tg) — apply at least 5 working days ahead (standard processing up to 5 working days), pay online only (Visa/Mastercard or TMoney/Flooz; cash is not accepted), and note that travellers without an approved visa are turned back at the border. Tourist visas are sold by duration: 1–15 days single entry 25,000 FCFA, 1–15 days multiple entry 35,000 FCFA, 16–30 days 45,000 FCFA and 31–90 days 65,000 FCFA — the 90 days shown is the maximum tourist stay. The e-Visa is valid at air, land and sea borders alike, and Togolese embassies no longer issue routine paper visas. A yellow-fever vaccination certificate is mandatory.

Tourist visas are sold by duration: 1–15 days single entry 25,000 FCFA, 1–15 days multiple entry 35,000 FCFA, 16–30 days 45,000 FCFA and 31–90 days 65,000 FCFA — the 90 days shown is the maximum tourist stay. The e-Visa is valid at air, land and sea borders alike, and Togolese embassies no longer issue routine paper visas. A yellow-fever vaccination certificate is mandatory.

Tourist visas are sold by duration: 1–15 days single entry 25,000 FCFA, 1–15 days multiple entry 35,000 FCFA, 16–30 days 45,000 FCFA and 31–90 days 65,000 FCFA — the 90 days shown is the maximum tourist stay. The e-Visa is valid at air, land and sea borders alike, and Togolese embassies no longer issue routine paper visas. A yellow-fever vaccination certificate is mandatory.

RW:TG.source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Togo — visa exemption for African nationals (May 2026)
RW:TG.note: Rwanda citizens are visa-exempt under Togo's decree of 26 May 2026, which exempts nationals of all African states holding a valid passport for stays of up to 30 days; stays beyond 30 days require an e-Visa obtained in advance on voyage.gouv.tg. The platform's static country tables predate the decree and still list Rwanda among the e-Visa countries. A bilateral ordinary-passport waiver with Togo has been reported in the media but is not officially confirmed; the exemption shown rests on the 2026 decree. Like all arrivals, exempt travellers must still complete the free immigration formalities online on voyage.gouv.tg before travelling — under the 2026 decree the travel declaration must be filed at least 24 hours before arrival to obtain the bordereau presented at the border post. A yellow-fever vaccination certificate is mandatory.

AD:CV.note: Andorra is on the Cabo Verde government portal's list of visa-exempt countries, with a maximum stay of 30 days. Before travelling, Andorra passport holders must pre-register on the EASE portal and pay the airport security tax (TSA, 3,400 CVE online); since 1 July 2026, travellers who arrive without proof of pre-registration pay double the TSA at the border.

AE:CV.source_name: Boletim Oficial n.º 14, II Série (23 Jan 2026) — Extrato do Despacho n.º 244/GMAI/2026 (Interior Ministry)
AE:CV.note: United Arab Emirates appears on neither of Cabo Verde's official lists: it is not in the government portal's visa-exempt table, and it is not in the annex to Interior Ministry Despacho n.º 244/GMAI/2026, which since 1 January 2026 names every nationality that must hold a visa before arrival. United Arab Emirates passport holders can therefore obtain a visa on arrival (Visto de Fronteira) at Cabo Verde's international airports and seaports. Cabo Verde publishes no consolidated border-visa list, fee or maximum stay for this channel, so the stay is set by the visa issued. EASE pre-registration and the airport security tax (TSA, 3,400 CVE online; doubled at the border since 1 July 2026 without proof of pre-registration) apply to all travellers.

AF:CV.source_name: Boletim Oficial n.º 14, II Série (23 Jan 2026) — Extrato do Despacho n.º 244/GMAI/2026 (Interior Ministry)
AF:CV.note: Since 1 January 2026, Afghanistan is in the annex to Interior Ministry Despacho n.º 244/GMAI/2026 (Boletim Oficial n.º 14, II Série, 23 January 2026): Afghanistan passport holders must obtain a visa from a Cabo Verdean embassy or consulate before travelling — entry, transit and airport stopovers without one are refused. The order publishes no maximum stay and no consular fee. The order does not apply to annex nationals who hold a valid residence permit issued by an EU member state, Iceland, Liechtenstein, the United Kingdom, San Marino, Switzerland, the Vatican, Brazil, Canada or the United States that guarantees unconditional readmission (section III.3(b)), nor to air crew, Cabo Verde foreign-resident card (TRE) holders and the other cases in section III.3. EASE pre-registration and the airport security tax (TSA, 3,400 CVE) apply to all incoming travellers regardless of visa status.

BH:CV.source_name: Boletim Oficial n.º 14, II Série (23 Jan 2026) — Extrato do Despacho n.º 244/GMAI/2026 (Interior Ministry)
BH:CV.note: Since 1 January 2026, Bahrain is in the annex to Interior Ministry Despacho n.º 244/GMAI/2026 (Boletim Oficial n.º 14, II Série, 23 January 2026): Bahrain passport holders must obtain a visa from a Cabo Verdean embassy or consulate before travelling — entry, transit and airport stopovers without one are refused. The order publishes no maximum stay and no consular fee. The order does not apply to annex nationals who hold a valid residence permit issued by an EU member state, Iceland, Liechtenstein, the United Kingdom, San Marino, Switzerland, the Vatican, Brazil, Canada or the United States that guarantees unconditional readmission (section III.3(b)), nor to air crew, Cabo Verde foreign-resident card (TRE) holders and the other cases in section III.3. EASE pre-registration and the airport security tax (TSA, 3,400 CVE) apply to all incoming travellers regardless of visa status.

The order does not apply to annex nationals who hold a valid residence permit issued by an EU member state, Iceland, Liechtenstein, the United Kingdom, San Marino, Switzerland, the Vatican, Brazil, Canada or the United States that guarantees unconditional readmission (section III.3(b)), nor to air crew, Cabo Verde foreign-resident card (TRE) holders and the other cases in section III.3. EASE pre-registration and the airport security tax (TSA, 3,400 CVE) apply to all incoming travellers regardless of visa status.

The order does not apply to annex nationals who hold a valid residence permit issued by an EU member state, Iceland, Liechtenstein, the United Kingdom, San Marino, Switzerland, the Vatican, Brazil, Canada or the United States that guarantees unconditional readmission (section III.3(b)), nor to air crew, Cabo Verde foreign-resident card (TRE) holders and the other cases in section III.3. EASE pre-registration and the airport security tax (TSA, 3,400 CVE) apply to all incoming travellers regardless of visa status.

AD:NG.source_name: Nigeria Immigration Service — Tourism Visa (F5A) page
AD:NG.note: Andorra passport holders apply for a Nigerian e-Visa before travel at evisa.immigration.gov.ng. The standard short-visit e-Visa (tourism F5A or single-entry business F4A) is valid for 90 days from issuance and allows a single stay of up to 30 days; it cannot be extended and cannot be converted into a work or residence permit in Nigeria. Visas on arrival were abolished on 1 May 2025, when the e-Visa system launched. Every traveller must also file the free electronic Landing Card at lecard.immigration.gov.ng before arrival (and an Exit Card before departure). Visa fees follow the reciprocity principle and are generated inside the e-Visa portal; no public per-country fee table exists. Some Nigerian mission pages still carry older tourist-visa wording allowing up to 90 days; the Immigration Service's current e-Visa pages set the stay at 30 days, and that figure is followed here.

Visas on arrival were abolished on 1 May 2025, when the e-Visa system launched. Every traveller must also file the free electronic Landing Card at lecard.immigration.gov.ng before arrival (and an Exit Card before departure). Visa fees follow the reciprocity principle and are generated inside the e-Visa portal; no public per-country fee table exists. Some Nigerian mission pages still carry older tourist-visa wording allowing up to 90 days; the Immigration Service's current e-Visa pages set the stay at 30 days, and that figure is followed here.

NE:NG.source_name: ECOWAS Commission — press statement of 29 January 2025
NE:NG.note: Niger is visa-free for Nigeria. Niger withdrew from ECOWAS effective 29 January 2025, but the ECOWAS Commission's statement of that date requires member states to continue to allow citizens of the three withdrawing states visa-free movement, residence and establishment until further notice. That statement covers passports bearing the ECOWAS logo; Nigeria has published nothing on the treatment of the new AES-logo passports, so holders of those should confirm before travel. Nigeria publishes no maximum stay for this exemption, so no duration is shown.

The standard short-visit e-Visa (tourism F5A or single-entry business F4A) is valid for 90 days from issuance and allows a single stay of up to 30 days; it cannot be extended and cannot be converted into a work or residence permit in Nigeria. Visas on arrival were abolished on 1 May 2025, when the e-Visa system launched. Every traveller must also file the free electronic Landing Card at lecard.immigration.gov.ng before arrival (and an Exit Card before departure). Visa fees follow the reciprocity principle and are generated inside the e-Visa portal; no public per-country fee table exists. Some Nigerian mission pages still carry older tourist-visa wording allowing up to 90 days; the Immigration Service's current e-Visa pages set the stay at 30 days, and that figure is followed here.

AF:MA.source_name: Morocco — Accès Maroc e-Visa terms (Categories B/C)
AF:MA.note: Afghanistan passport holders need a visa before travel to Morocco; there is no general visa on arrival (a border-issued visa exists only in exceptional cases at the discretion of the border authorities). If you hold a residence permit valid at least 180 days from a qualifying place (EU, US, Australia, Canada, UK, Japan, Norway, New Zealand, UAE, Switzerland) or a non-electronic multiple-entry visa valid at least 90 days from a qualifying place (Schengen, US, Australia, Canada, UK, Ireland, Japan, Norway, New Zealand), you may instead apply for the conditional e-Visa at acces-maroc.ma (single entry, stay up to 30 days, validity up to 180 days). Otherwise apply at the Moroccan embassy or consulate for your place of residence (short-stay consular visas are generally up to 90 days; transit visas up to 72 hours).

AD:DZ.source_name: Consulate of Algeria in Agadez — entry visa to Algeria (Algerian MFA)
AD:DZ.note: Andorra passport holders must obtain a visa from an Algerian diplomatic or consular post before travel; Algeria has no general e-Visa portal for ordinary tourists or business travellers and no walk-up visa on arrival for ordinary northern itineraries. Apply at the consulate of your usual place of residence with a passport valid at least 6 months, two photos, an accommodation certificate certified by the local town hall (or a hotel booking / travel-agency itinerary) and travel insurance (required for listed nationalities; not for British and Irish citizens at the London consulate). Processing at the London consulate is generally 10 working days in person (at least 15 by post) with no express service; fees vary by nationality and consulate (London: £85 standard, £270 work/temporary work, £60 transit). Direct airside transit at Algiers airport within 24 hours without passing immigration may not need a transit visa — confirm with your airline; any landside transit needs a consular transit visa (stopover permits of 2 to 7 days are issued by Algerian consulates). Exception — organised southern Sahara tours: travellers on a tour booked through a licensed Algerian agency, with most of the travel in the south (24 southern provinces), may obtain a visa on arrival under the Visa de régularisation scheme: the agency submits documents at least 15–20 days ahead, the Interior Ministry issues a QR-coded boarding authorisation to present at check-in, and the visa is issued on arrival for up to 30 days (fee in cash on arrival).

Apply at the consulate of your usual place of residence with a passport valid at least 6 months, two photos, an accommodation certificate certified by the local town hall (or a hotel booking / travel-agency itinerary) and travel insurance (required for listed nationalities; not for British and Irish citizens at the London consulate). Processing at the London consulate is generally 10 working days in person (at least 15 by post) with no express service; fees vary by nationality and consulate (London: £85 standard, £270 work/temporary work, £60 transit). Direct airside transit at Algiers airport within 24 hours without passing immigration may not need a transit visa — confirm with your airline; any landside transit needs a consular transit visa (stopover permits of 2 to 7 days are issued by Algerian consulates). Exception — organised southern Sahara tours: travellers on a tour booked through a licensed Algerian agency, with most of the travel in the south (24 southern provinces), may obtain a visa on arrival under the Visa de régularisation scheme: the agency submits documents at least 15–20 days ahead, the Interior Ministry issues a QR-coded boarding authorisation to present at check-in, and the visa is issued on arrival for up to 30 days (fee in cash on arrival).

Processing at the London consulate is generally 10 working days in person (at least 15 by post) with no express service; fees vary by nationality and consulate (London: £85 standard, £270 work/temporary work, £60 transit). AF:TN.source_name: Visa policy of Tunisia (Timatic-based exemption table; Berlin embassy + Timatic refs)
AF:TN.note: Afghanistan passport holders must obtain a visa from a Tunisian diplomatic or consular post before travel; Tunisia has no official e-Visa portal (the 2024 tender was declared unsuccessful in August 2025, and third-party 'e-Visa' sites are intermediaries) and no general visa on arrival. Tourist applications require the Interior Minister's approval; the Washington embassy requires a passport valid at least 6 months, a hotel reservation or notarised invitation, and charges $90 single / $180 multiple (non-refundable, money order only), with processing up to 21 business days. Direct airside transit within 24 hours without entering Tunisia may not need a transit visa — confirm with your airline; any landside transit needs a consular transit visa. Passport validity guidance varies: the UK advises validity for the duration of stay, France at least 3 months on entry, and consular visa applications require 6 months.

TN:LY.source_name: Visa policy of Libya (Timatic-based exemption table)

MY:LY.source_name: Visa policy of Libya (Timatic-based exemption table)

AD:LY.source_name: Visa policy of Libya (Timatic-based exemption table)
AD:LY.note: Andorra passport holders must obtain a Libyan visa before travel. Apply through the official e-Visa portal at evisa.gov.ly before travel. The tourist e-Visa is single-entry, valid 90 days from issue and allows a stay of up to 30 days (fee US$63). A sponsor is required: tourists must travel on a package booked through a licensed Libyan tour operator, or hold a local sponsor with a security letter from the Libyan immigration authorities; independent tourist travel is generally not allowed and a tourist-police escort applies. Register with the authorities within 7 days of arrival and hold a passport valid at least 6 months beyond departure.

Jordan also has a December 2024 arrangement (Prime Minister's Decision No. 590/2024) for a visa on arrival at Mitiga and Misurata airports, but Libya suspended airport visa-on-arrival issuance on 11 June 2026 and no official resumption has been published, so the e-Visa channel is the settled route here. A sponsor is required: tourists must travel on a package booked through a licensed Libyan tour operator, or hold a local sponsor with a security letter from the Libyan immigration authorities; a security letter may be required for Jordanian nationals in particular.

The tourist e-Visa is single-entry, valid 90 days from issue and allows a stay of up to 30 days (fee US$63). A sponsor is required: tourists must travel on a package booked through a licensed Libyan tour operator, or hold a local sponsor with a security letter from the Libyan immigration authorities; independent tourist travel is generally not allowed and a tourist-police escort applies. Register with the authorities within 7 days of arrival and hold a passport valid at least 6 months beyond departure.

The tourist e-Visa is single-entry, valid 90 days from issue and allows a stay of up to 30 days (fee US$63). A sponsor is required: tourists must travel on a package booked through a licensed Libyan tour operator, or hold a local sponsor with a security letter from the Libyan immigration authorities; independent tourist travel is generally not allowed and a tourist-police escort applies. Register with the authorities within 7 days of arrival and hold a passport valid at least 6 months beyond departure.

IL:LY.source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Serbia — Libya visa regime (quoting Law No. 6 of 1987 implementing regulations)
IL:LY.note: Israeli passport holders are not admitted to Libya, for entry or for transit — even airside without leaving the aircraft. Visitors of any nationality are also refused entry or transit if they hold an Israeli travel document, an Israeli visa, or any evidence of having entered Israel (stamp or otherwise). The ban rests on Libya's 1957 boycott law and on the implementing regulations of Law No. 6 of 1987, which bar entry visas to persons holding Israeli travel documents, Israeli entry visas, or confirmed entry into Israel. The e-Visa portal does not accept Israeli nationality.

AD:EG.source_name: Wikipedia — Visa policy of Egypt (IATA Timatic)
AD:EG.note: Visa on arrival for tourism, up to 30 days. Buy at the airport before immigration for US$30 in cash; since August 2026 Cairo airport also sells a US$36 digital QR visa (card payment) via self-service machines or the Visa on Arrival portal. Your passport must be valid at least 6 months beyond arrival and have at least one blank page.

AE:EG.source_name: Wikipedia — Visa policy of Egypt (IATA Timatic)
AE:EG.note: Visa-free for up to 6 months. Your passport must be valid at least 6 months beyond arrival.

AF:EG.source_name: Embassy of Egypt in Washington — visa requirements
AF:EG.note: A visa must be obtained in advance with pre-approval from Egypt: applications are by email only, walk-ins are not accepted, and the Washington embassy quotes a minimum of 6–8 weeks for the first stage. Do not make travel plans until approval is received. Pre-approval nationals cannot obtain any visa on arrival, including holders of a US green card. In addition to the visa, Afghan nationals must hold confirmation from Egypt’s Ministry of Interior that entry has been approved before departure. A Timatic age-based exemption (under 16 or over 50) is superseded by the embassy’s all-national pre-approval rule.

AD:IL.source_name: Wikipedia - Visa policy of Israel (Timatic-based exemption table; ETA-IL rules per gov.il/PIBA)
AD:IL.note: Visa-exempt for up to 90 days (30 days for culture or sport activities). An approved ETA-IL is mandatory before travel since 1 January 2025: apply via the PIBA portal at least 72 hours ahead (fee ILS 25, valid 2 years or to passport expiry, multiple entries). Approval does not guarantee entry; the border officer decides. Passport validity: 3 months beyond arrival is the official ETA-IL rule, but airlines commonly enforce 6 months, so carry 6 months to be safe. An in-country extension of up to 90 days may be applied for.

AF:IL.source_name: Israel MFA - Tourist Visa Table (2022), cross-checked against the October 2026 exemption/eVisa lists
AF:IL.note: Obtain a visa in advance, but the mission cannot issue it alone: every application must be referred to the MFA in Jerusalem for pre-approval and security clearance. There is no fixed processing cap; allow weeks to months. Passport must be valid 6 months beyond arrival.

AG:IL.source_name: Israel MFA - Tourist Visa Table (2022), cross-checked against the October 2026 exemption/eVisa lists
AG:IL.note: Obtain a B/2 visitor visa in advance from an Israeli mission; stays of up to 90 days. Fee around ILS 100 (the mission charges the local equivalent). Processing is typically 5-14 working days and may require an interview. Passport must be valid 6 months beyond arrival.

An approved ETA-IL is mandatory before travel since 1 January 2025: apply via the PIBA portal at least 72 hours ahead (fee ILS 25, valid 2 years or to passport expiry, multiple entries). Approval does not guarantee entry; the border officer decides. Passport validity: 3 months beyond arrival is the official ETA-IL rule, but airlines commonly enforce 6 months, so carry 6 months to be safe. An in-country extension of up to 90 days may be applied for.

PK:IL.source_name: Israel MFA - Tourist Visa Table (2022), cross-checked against the October 2026 exemption/eVisa lists
PK:IL.note: Obtain a visa in advance, but the mission cannot issue it alone: every application must be referred to the MFA in Jerusalem for pre-approval and security clearance. There is no fixed processing cap; allow weeks to months. Passport must be valid 6 months beyond arrival.

PS:IL.source_name: GOV.UK - Palestine travel advice: entry requirements (COGAT permit regime per research report)
PS:IL.note: Entry for holders of Palestinian passports is not via an ordinary tourist visa: it is governed by COGAT permits tied to the Palestinian population register. Holders registered in the West Bank or Gaza must obtain the applicable COGAT permit in advance (the research report cites a 45-day application rule for some permit classes, a 27-month cumulative cap and a 6-month cooling period in the dual-track regime); exit from the West Bank or Gaza is normally only via the Allenby Bridge crossing into Jordan or the Rafah crossing into Egypt, returning by the same route. This pair is classified as visa-required because no walk-up or online tourist-visa route exists for this passport as such; the permit, not a consular B/2 visa, is the channel. A holder of a Palestinian passport alone has no ordinary route into Israel proper or through an Israeli airport without a COGAT Entry Permit; the “Judea and Samaria only” B/2 is a West Bank-area permit, not a tourist visa for Israel proper. The population-register lock follows the registration, not the passport in hand: a person registered with a PA ID is excluded from ordinary foreign-citizen entry rules even if they also hold an exempt foreign passport, and must normally travel on Palestinian documents via the Allenby Bridge. Gaza’s regular channels are closed to ordinary visitors, with only case-by-case humanitarian or UN passage.

The same trip can instead be arranged in advance as an e-Visa (single 40 JOD, double 60 JOD, multiple 120 JOD). Stays beyond 30 days require registration at a local police station (unregistered overstay: 3 JOD per day). A Jordan Pass bought before arrival waives the 40 JOD fee for stays of at least 3 full nights (4 days); travellers using a licensed agency Meet & Assist service need only 2 nights. Walk-in visas on arrival are NOT issued at the King Hussein (Allenby) Bridge, and are restricted at the Wadi Araba crossing — e-Visa holders may use all ports.

SD:JO.source_name: Jordan Ministry of Interior — Restricted and Non-Restricted Countries
SD:JO.note: Sudan passports are on the Jordanian Ministry of Interior restricted list: entry requires prior approval from the Ministry (via the MOI e-services portal or a Jordanian mission) before travel — do not travel to a port expecting a visa on arrival. Processing is typically 0–14 working days (complex security or labour cases 30–60 days). A Jordanian sponsor may apply online (2 JOD service fee; sponsors usually post a 1,000 JOD financial guarantee). Holders of a residence permit from a GCC state, a Schengen state, the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Japan, South Korea, Cyprus or Ireland (at least 6 months remaining per the MOI e-services portal; carrier wording differs — 3 months issued and remaining) or a US green card, with a non-refundable return ticket and hotel booking, may instead obtain an e-Visa or a visa on arrival without prior approval. Medical-travel exception: males under 15 or aged 50 or over, and females of any age, travelling for treatment with a return ticket and a Jordanian hospital report, may obtain a visa on arrival without prior approval.

Fees are paid in cash (USD) at the border or airport; there is no working official e-Visa — evisa.sy stopped operating after December 2024. Carry a passport valid at least 6 months, a return ticket and a hotel booking or invitation; airlines may ask for proof of funds of about USD 100 per day. Refusal rule: any Israeli visa or stamp in the passport, or an Egyptian or Jordanian land-border stamp from a crossing adjoining Israel (Taba, Wadi Araba, Allenby/King Hussein Bridge), means refusal of entry and transit.

AD:PS.source_name: Wikipedia — Visa policy of Palestine (entry follows Israeli visa policy)
AD:PS.note: Entry to the West Bank follows Israeli visa policy: Palestine imposes no visa of its own. With an approved ETA-IL (ILS 25, valid 2 years, apply at least 72 hours ahead) you may enter Israel for up to 90 days and travel to the West Bank, subject to approval by a COGAT representative at the crossing on presentation of status and purpose documents. ETA-IL approval does not by itself guarantee West Bank entry. At Allenby Bridge (and sometimes Ben Gurion Airport) travellers may receive a ‘Palestinian Authority only’ / ‘Judea and Samaria only’ stamp limiting travel to PA-controlled areas; travelling into Israel-proper on such a stamp risks deportation and a bar of up to 10 years. At Ben Gurion some travellers are asked to sign a form barring PA-territory entry without COGAT advance authorisation. Travellers of Palestinian origin (on the Palestinian Population Register or holding a Palestinian ID number) must hold a Palestinian passport or travel document and may enter only via Allenby Bridge. Passports must be valid at least 90 days beyond arrival (GOV.UK). Gaza is a separate regime: entry needs a Hamas exit permit plus an Israeli entry permit, granted mainly for medical care and certain merchants, workers and students; the Erez crossing is currently closed and Rafah is unpredictable and needs prior Egyptian permission, so Gaza is effectively not open to ordinary tourists.

AD:CY.source_name: Wikipedia — Visa policy of the Schengen Area (Annex II list, adopted by Cyprus)
AD:CY.note: Visa-free for short stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period (Annex II of EU Regulation 2018/1806, adopted by Cyprus; the Cyprus 90/180 clock runs separately from the Schengen one). Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure and issued within the previous 10 years; border officers may ask for the purpose of the stay, sufficient funds and return or onward proof. Enter only through the Republic's legal ports of entry (Larnaca and Paphos airports and the seaports); entering via the north is treated as illegal entry by the Republic of Cyprus.

A uniform visa issued by any Schengen state is valid for Czechia, and holders of a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by another Schengen state may enter without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure, with two blank pages, issued within the previous 10 years.

A uniform visa issued by any Schengen state is valid for Denmark, and holders of a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by another Schengen state may enter without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure, with two blank pages, issued within the previous 10 years. This covers Denmark proper; the Faroe Islands and Greenland are not part of the Schengen Area and have separate entry rules.

Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure and issued within the previous 10 years; border officers may ask for the purpose of the stay, sufficient funds and return or onward proof.

LI:EE.source_name: Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Who does not need a visa to visit Estonia
LI:EE.note: Freedom of movement: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens may enter Estonia with a passport or a national identity card bearing a photo, and may live and work without a visa; no 90-day cap applies.

LK:EE.source_name: Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Who does not need a visa to visit Estonia
LK:EE.note: A short-stay Schengen (uniform) visa is required in advance from an Estonian consulate or visa application centre: fee EUR 90, apply between 6 months and at least 15 days before travel, decisions usually within 15 days (up to 45). A uniform visa issued by any Schengen state is valid for Estonia, and holders of a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by another Schengen state may enter without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure, with two blank pages, issued within the previous 10 years.

A uniform visa issued by any Schengen state is valid for Estonia, and holders of a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by another Schengen state may enter without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure, with two blank pages, issued within the previous 10 years.

SE:EE.source_name: Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Who does not need a visa to visit Estonia
SE:EE.note: Freedom of movement: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens may enter Estonia with a passport or a national identity card bearing a photo, and may live and work without a visa; no 90-day cap applies.

A uniform visa issued by any Schengen state is valid for Finland, and holders of a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by another Schengen state may enter without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure, with two blank pages, issued within the previous 10 years.

MT:FI.source_name: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland — A visa to visit Finland
MT:FI.note: Freedom of movement: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens may enter Finland with a passport or a national identity card bearing a photo, and may live and work without a visa; no 90-day cap applies.

MU:FI.source_name: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland — A visa to visit Finland
MU:FI.note: Visa-free for short stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen Area as a whole — the clock covers all Schengen states combined (Annex II of EU Regulation 2018/1806; the Schengen states jointly agree the list, per the Finnish MFA). Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure and issued within the previous 10 years; at the border expect to show the purpose of the stay, return or onward proof and funds of at least EUR 50 per day.

Visa-free entry does not permit taking up gainful employment. Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure and issued within the previous 10 years; border officers may ask for the purpose of the stay, sufficient funds and return or onward proof.

BT:DE.source_name: German Federal Foreign Office — Overview of visa requirements/exemptions for entry into Germany
BT:DE.note: A short-stay Schengen (uniform) visa is required in advance from a German embassy or consulate or its authorised service provider: fee EUR 90, apply between 6 months and at least 15 days before travel, decisions usually within 15 days (up to 45). A uniform visa issued by any Schengen state is valid for Germany, and holders of a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by another Schengen state may enter without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure, with two blank pages, issued within the previous 10 years.

A uniform visa issued by any Schengen state is valid for Italy, and holders of a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by another Schengen state may enter without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure, with two blank pages, issued within the previous 10 years.

Fee EUR 90; apply between 6 months and at least 15 days before travel. A uniform visa issued by any Schengen state is valid for the Netherlands, and holders of a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by another Schengen state may enter without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure, with two blank pages, issued within the previous 10 years. This covers the European part of the Netherlands; the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom (Aruba, Bonaire, Curaçao, Saba, Sint Eustatius and Sint Maarten) have their own entry rules.

EE:NL.source_name: Netherlands Schengen visa list (NederlandWereldwijd / IND) — Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806

This covers the European part of the Netherlands; the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom (Aruba, Bonaire, Curaçao, Saba, Sint Eustatius and Sint Maarten) have their own entry rules.

BD:AT.source_name: Austrian Federal Ministry for European and International Affairs (BMEIA) — Visum; EU exemption per Regulation (EU) 2018/1806
BD:AT.note: A short-stay Schengen (uniform) visa is required in advance from the Austrian embassy or consulate for your place of residence or its external service provider (where Austria has no representation, a representing Schengen embassy): fee EUR 90, apply between 6 months and at least 15 days before travel, decisions within 15 calendar days (up to 45). Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure, with two blank pages, issued within the previous 10 years.

AD:HU.source_name: Hungarian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade — Consular information (Konzinfo): Short Term Stay; EU exemption per Regulation (EU) 2018/1806
AD:HU.note: Visa-free for short stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen Area as a whole — the clock covers all Schengen states combined (Annex II of EU Regulation 2018/1806). Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure and issued within the previous 10 years; border officers may ask for the purpose of the stay, sufficient funds and return or onward proof.

AE:HU.source_name: Hungarian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade — Consular information (Konzinfo): Short Term Stay; EU exemption per Regulation (EU) 2018/1806
AE:HU.note: Visa-free for short stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen Area as a whole — the clock covers all Schengen states combined (Annex II of EU Regulation 2018/1806). AF:HU.source_name: Hungarian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade — Consular information (Konzinfo): Short Term Stay; EU exemption per Regulation (EU) 2018/1806
AF:HU.note: A short-stay Schengen (uniform) visa is required in advance from the Hungarian embassy or consulate for your place of residence (where a Member State represents Hungary, its mission; if there is neither, any Hungarian consulate outside the Schengen Area): fee EUR 90, apply between 6 months and at least 15 days before travel, decisions within 15 calendar days (up to 45; 10 days under EU facilitation agreements); travel medical insurance covering at least EUR 30,000 is required. A uniform visa issued by any Schengen state is valid for Hungary, and holders of a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by another Schengen state may enter without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure, with two blank pages, issued within the previous 10 years. Hungary also requires an airport transit visa from this nationality for passing through the international zone of a Hungarian airport.

Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure and issued within the previous 10 years; border officers may ask for the purpose of the stay, sufficient funds and return or onward proof. Applies to holders of the Special Administrative Region passport only.

HR:HU.source_name: Hungarian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade — Consular information (Konzinfo): Short Term Stay; EU exemption per Regulation (EU) 2018/1806
HR:HU.note: Freedom of movement: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens may enter Hungary with a passport or a national identity card bearing a photo, and may live and work without a visa; no 90-day cap applies.

HT:HU.source_name: Hungarian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade — Consular information (Konzinfo): Short Term Stay; EU exemption per Regulation (EU) 2018/1806
HT:HU.note: A short-stay Schengen (uniform) visa is required in advance from the Hungarian embassy or consulate for your place of residence (where a Member State represents Hungary, its mission; if there is neither, any Hungarian consulate outside the Schengen Area): fee EUR 90, apply between 6 months and at least 15 days before travel, decisions within 15 calendar days (up to 45; 10 days under EU facilitation agreements); travel medical insurance covering at least EUR 30,000 is required. A uniform visa issued by any Schengen state is valid for Hungary, and holders of a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by another Schengen state may enter without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure, with two blank pages, issued within the previous 10 years.

A uniform visa issued by any Schengen state is valid for Iceland, and holders of a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by another Schengen state may enter without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure, with two blank pages, issued within the previous 10 years.

LI:IS.source_name: Directorate of Immigration (Ísland.is) — Entry requirements to Iceland and the official visa checker; Government of Iceland — Visit Iceland; EU exemption per Regulation (EU) 2018/1806

Nordic citizens travelling between Iceland and Denmark, Finland, Norway or Sweden are exempt even from the travel-document requirement at the border.
