Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure and issued within the previous 10 years; border officers may ask for the purpose of the stay, sufficient funds and return or onward proof. Liechtenstein has no airport of its own — entry is overland from Switzerland or Austria, with no border checks on those routes.

CD:LI.source_name: Liechtenstein Migration and Passport Office (Ausländer- und Passamt) — Visum page (llv.li); EU exemption per Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 via the EEA/Schengen association
CD:LI.note: A short-stay Schengen (uniform) visa is required in advance. Liechtenstein does not issue visas itself: apply at the Swiss embassy or consulate for your place of residence — in a few locations another Schengen state represents Liechtenstein, and the Migration and Passport Office (Auslaender- und Passamt) publishes the list; the decision lies partly with the Swiss authorities and partly with that Office. Fee EUR 90, apply between 6 months and at least 15 days before travel, decisions within 15 calendar days (up to 45). A uniform visa issued by any Schengen state is valid for Liechtenstein, and holders of a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by another Schengen state may enter without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure, issued within the previous 10 years. Liechtenstein has no airport of its own — entry is overland from Switzerland or Austria, with no border checks on those routes.

Liechtenstein does not issue visas itself: apply at the Swiss embassy or consulate for your place of residence — in a few locations another Schengen state represents Liechtenstein, and the Migration and Passport Office (Auslaender- und Passamt) publishes the list; the decision lies partly with the Swiss authorities and partly with that Office. Fee EUR 90, apply between 6 months and at least 15 days before travel, decisions within 15 calendar days (up to 45). A uniform visa issued by any Schengen state is valid for Liechtenstein, and holders of a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by another Schengen state may enter without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure, issued within the previous 10 years. Liechtenstein has no airport of its own — entry is overland from Switzerland or Austria, with no border checks on those routes.

Liechtenstein does not issue visas itself: apply at the Swiss embassy or consulate for your place of residence — in a few locations another Schengen state represents Liechtenstein, and the Migration and Passport Office (Auslaender- und Passamt) publishes the list; the decision lies partly with the Swiss authorities and partly with that Office. Fee EUR 90, apply between 6 months and at least 15 days before travel, decisions within 15 calendar days (up to 45). A uniform visa issued by any Schengen state is valid for Liechtenstein, and holders of a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by another Schengen state may enter without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure, issued within the previous 10 years. Liechtenstein has no airport of its own — entry is overland from Switzerland or Austria, with no border checks on those routes.

Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure and issued within the previous 10 years; border officers may ask for the purpose of the stay, sufficient funds and return or onward proof. Liechtenstein has no airport of its own — entry is overland from Switzerland or Austria, with no border checks on those routes.

XK:LI.source_name: Liechtenstein Migration and Passport Office (Ausländer- und Passamt) — Visum page (llv.li); EU exemption per Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 via the EEA/Schengen association
XK:LI.note: Visa-free for short stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen Area as a whole — the clock covers all Schengen states combined (Annex II of EU Regulation 2018/1806, which Liechtenstein applies through its Schengen association). Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure and issued within the previous 10 years; border officers may ask for the purpose of the stay, sufficient funds and return or onward proof. Liechtenstein has no airport of its own — entry is overland from Switzerland or Austria, with no border checks on those routes. Biometric passports only — holders of non-biometric passports need a visa in advance.

YE:LI.source_name: Liechtenstein Migration and Passport Office (Ausländer- und Passamt) — Visum page (llv.li); EU exemption per Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 via the EEA/Schengen association
YE:LI.note: A short-stay Schengen (uniform) visa is required in advance. Liechtenstein does not issue visas itself: apply at the Swiss embassy or consulate for your place of residence — in a few locations another Schengen state represents Liechtenstein, and the Migration and Passport Office (Auslaender- und Passamt) publishes the list; the decision lies partly with the Swiss authorities and partly with that Office. Fee EUR 90, apply between 6 months and at least 15 days before travel, decisions within 15 calendar days (up to 45). A uniform visa issued by any Schengen state is valid for Liechtenstein, and holders of a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by another Schengen state may enter without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure, issued within the previous 10 years. Liechtenstein has no airport of its own — entry is overland from Switzerland or Austria, with no border checks on those routes.

AD:US.source_name: U.S. Department of State — Visa Waiver Program
AD:US.note: Travel under the Visa Waiver Program (VWP): get an ESTA authorisation from CBP online before boarding — fee USD 40.62 since 16 October 2026 (USD 40 from 30 September 2025, USD 21 before that); an approved ESTA is normally valid for two years or until the passport expires. Stays of up to 90 days for tourism or business; the stay cannot be extended and status cannot be changed, and an approved ESTA does not guarantee admission — the CBP officer at the port of entry decides. An e-passport is required. Travellers who have been in North Korea, Iran, Iraq, Libya, Somalia, Sudan, Syria or Yemen on or after 1 March 2011, or in Cuba on or after 12 January 2021, and dual nationals of Cuba, North Korea, Iran, Iraq, Sudan or Syria, cannot use the VWP and need a visitor visa instead.

AF:US.source_name: Presidential Proclamation 10998 of 16 December 2025 (Federal Register, 19 December 2025)
AF:US.note: Entry is fully suspended. Under Presidential Proclamation 10949 (in force since 9 June 2025), continued in force by Proclamation 10998 from 1 January 2026, the entry of nationals of Afghanistan as immigrants and as nonimmigrants is suspended and U.S. consulates are not issuing them visas, subject only to narrow exceptions (such as diplomatic visas, lawful permanent residents, and dual nationals travelling on a passport of an unaffected country). Visas validly issued before the suspension took effect were not revoked by the proclamations.

AG:US.source_name: Presidential Proclamation 10998 of 16 December 2025 (Federal Register, 19 December 2025)
AG:US.note: Entry is partially suspended. Under Presidential Proclamation 10998 (in force since 1 January 2026), the United States is not issuing immigrant visas or B-1/B-2 visitor, F, M or J visas to nationals of Antigua & Barbuda; other nonimmigrant categories remain possible, with their validity liable to be shortened by the consular officer. The restriction was added by that proclamation. Antigua & Barbuda is also on the Department of State's visa bond list: an applicant found otherwise eligible for a B-1/B-2 visa must post a refundable bond of USD 10,000, 15,000 or 20,000, set by the consular officer at the interview (programme made permanent by the Final Rule of 3 August 2026; Form I-352, paid via Pay.gov).

AL:US.source_name: U.S. Department of State — Visa Waiver Program
AL:US.note: A visitor visa (B-1/B-2) is required in advance: complete Form DS-160 online and attend an interview at a U.S. embassy or consulate; the application fee is USD 185 and is non-refundable. Visa validity and number of entries follow the reciprocity schedule for Albania; at each entry the CBP officer sets the authorised stay (up to six months for visitors).

MT:US.source_name: U.S. Department of State — Visa Waiver Program

AD:GB.source_name: Immigration Rules Appendix ETA National List (GOV.UK)
AD:GB.note: Get an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) online or in the UK ETA app before travelling — fee £20 since 8 April 2026 (£16 from 9 April 2025, £10 at launch). An approved ETA is valid for 2 years or until the passport expires, allows multiple journeys, and each stay as a Visitor may be up to 6 months. An ETA is permission to travel, not a guarantee of admission — the Border Force officer decides on arrival. Apply on the passport you will travel with. Since 25 February 2026 carriers must check permission to travel before boarding. Coming to marry, form a civil partnership or give notice of marriage in the UK always needs a Marriage/Civil Partnership Visitor visa in advance — an ETA does not cover it.

AD:JP.source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan — Exemption of Visa (Short-Term Stay)
AD:JP.note: No visa is required for a short-term stay of up to 90 days for tourism, business or visiting friends or relatives. Landing permission is granted by an immigration officer on arrival; a visa exemption does not guarantee entry.

AF:JP.source_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan — VISA

ID:CN.source_name: National Immigration Administration — Visa-Free Transit Policy (240-hour scheme, 57 countries; Hainan scheme, 61 countries)
ID:CN.note: A Chinese visa is required in advance — apply through a Chinese Visa Application Service Center or a Chinese embassy or consulate (fees, validity and number of entries vary by nationality and reciprocity). Most nationalities can transit China airside for up to 24 hours without a visa, but a visa is always needed to enter China as the destination; work, study and residence need the matching visa category. Indonesia is one of the 57 nationalities eligible for China's 240-hour (10-day) visa-free transit: with a confirmed onward ticket to a third country or territory, travellers may enter at 65 designated ports across 24 provinces and stay within the designated areas for up to 240 hours — for transit only, not for visiting China as the destination. Separately, Indonesia passport holders may enter Hainan Province without a visa for up to 30 days under the Hainan visa-free scheme (61 countries) — valid for Hainan only, not for the rest of mainland China.

HK:CA.source_name: IRCC — Check if you need a visa or eTA to travel to Canada
HK:CA.note: Hong Kong SAR China passport holders do not need a visitor visa for Canada. When flying to Canada, get an electronic travel authorization (eTA) before boarding — apply online on the Government of Canada site (CAD 7, electronically linked to the passport, valid for up to 5 years). Arriving by land or sea needs no eTA, just the passport. A border officer admits visitors for up to 6 months. This covers passports issued by the Hong Kong SAR.

BY:CA.source_name: IRCC — Check if you need a visa or eTA to travel to Canada
BY:CA.note: Belarus passport holders need a visitor visa (a temporary resident visa) for Canada, however they arrive — by air, land or sea. Apply online to IRCC before travelling: CAD 100 per person, plus CAD 85 for biometrics for most applicants aged 14 to 79. A border officer decides the length of each stay, up to 6 months.

Apply online to IRCC before travelling: CAD 100 per person, plus CAD 85 for biometrics for most applicants aged 14 to 79. A border officer decides the length of each stay, up to 6 months.

SB:CA.source_name: IRCC — Check if you need a visa or eTA to travel to Canada
SB:CA.note: Solomon Islands passport holders do not need a visitor visa for Canada. When flying to Canada, get an electronic travel authorization (eTA) before boarding — apply online on the Government of Canada site (CAD 7, electronically linked to the passport, valid for up to 5 years). Arriving by land or sea needs no eTA, just the passport. A border officer admits visitors for up to 6 months.

Apply online to IRCC before travelling: CAD 100 per person, plus CAD 85 for biometrics for most applicants aged 14 to 79. A border officer decides the length of each stay, up to 6 months. Exception: if you fly to Canada and have held a Canadian visitor visa in the past 10 years, or hold a valid US nonimmigrant visa, you may apply for an eTA (CAD 7) instead of a visa — arriving by land or sea still needs the visa.

TR:CH.source_name: Swiss State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) — entry requirements & Annex CH-1 nationality list; Regulation (EU) 2018/1806
TR:CH.note: Türkiye passport holders need a Schengen visa for Switzerland (type C, up to 90 days in any 180-day period), applied for at the Swiss embassy or consulate or via its external service provider (swiss-visa.ch); the standard fee is EUR 90 and decisions normally take 15 days. Türkiye nationals also need an airport transit visa to pass through the international transit area of a Swiss airport.

NP:SE.source_name: Swedish Migration Agency (Migrationsverket) — Apply for a Schengen visa; EU exemption per Regulation (EU) 2018/1806
NP:SE.note: Nepal passport holders need a short-stay Schengen (uniform) visa in advance: apply at a VFS Global centre or a Swedish embassy or consulate-general — in a number of countries another Schengen state represents Sweden (fee EUR 90; lodge up to 6 months before travel; Sweden requires means of SEK 700 per day and travel medical insurance of at least EUR 30,000). A uniform visa issued by any Schengen state is valid for Sweden, and holders of a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by another Schengen state may enter without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.

Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure and issued within the previous 10 years. Biometric passports only — holders of non-biometric passports need a visa in advance (EUR 35 under the EU visa facilitation agreement).

Passport must be valid at least 3 months after the intended departure and issued within the previous 10 years. Biometric passports only — holders of non-biometric passports need a visa in advance (EUR 35 under the EU visa facilitation agreement). Passports issued by the Serbian Coordination Directorate for Kosovo and Metohija are covered since 13 October 2024.

A uniform visa issued by any Schengen state is valid for Slovakia, and holders of a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by another Schengen state may enter without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Slovakia also requires an airport transit visa from this nationality for passing through a Slovak airport, unless the traveller holds a residence permit issued by a Schengen state valid at least 3 months beyond the transit.

MG:HR.note: Madagascar passport holders need a short-stay Schengen (uniform) visa in advance: apply at a Croatian diplomatic mission or a VFS Global centre (fee EUR 90; lodge up to 6 months before travel; travel medical insurance of at least EUR 30,000 and sufficient means of subsistence are required).
